crops.name: Strawberry
crops.ireland: Irish commercial crop is mostly under tunnels/table-tops (Wexford strawberries are famous).

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Compost before planting; seaweed/potash-rich organic feed in flowering.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Regular moisture; most commercial crops in Ireland use trickle irrigation and tunnels/table-tops.

harvest.storage: Very short: pick into the cool, eat within 2–3 days.

conventional.pests: Botrytis (grey mould), powdery mildew, aphids, vine weevil, slugs, birds, red spider mite.

organic.pests: Straw or mat mulch, wider spacing, biological controls (Phytoseiulus, nematodes for vine weevil), resistant varieties, netting, renew plants every 3 years.
organic.weeds: Mulch film or straw, hand weeding.

crops.rotation: 3-year plantings; 1 in 4–5 years on the same soil (verticillium).

crops.name: Raspberry
crops.ireland: Thrives in cool Irish summers; avoid wet heavy soil (root rot).

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.5–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Compost/FYM mulch each spring; blackcurrants are hungry, gooseberries need potash.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.5–6.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Mulch and water in dry spells, especially when fruit swells.

harvest.storage: Pick and chill; freeze or jam.

conventional.pests: Raspberry beetle, cane spot, spur blight, root rot (Phytophthora) on wet soil, botrytis, viruses.

organic.pests: Plant certified virus-free canes on raised beds on heavier soils, remove old canes, good airflow, resistant varieties, pheromone-free beetle traps (white sticky).
organic.weeds: Heavy mulch, hand weeding; clear perennial weeds before planting.

crops.rotation: Plantations last 8–12 years; do not replant on the same ground.

crops.name: Blackcurrant
crops.ireland: Very well suited; choose big-bud-mite and mildew-resistant Ben varieties.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

planting.window: Nov–Mar, plant 5 cm deeper than before

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–6.7; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Compost/FYM mulch each spring; blackcurrants are hungry, gooseberries need potash.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–6.7; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Mulch and water in dry spells, especially when fruit swells.

harvest.storage: Pick and chill; freeze or jam.

conventional.pests: Gooseberry sawfly, aphids, big bud mite (blackcurrant), American gooseberry mildew, leaf spot, birds.

organic.pests: Resistant varieties (e.g. Ben series blackcurrants, Invicta gooseberry), hand-pick sawfly larvae, net against birds, open pruning for airflow.
organic.weeds: Heavy mulch, hand weeding; clear perennial weeds before planting.

crops.rotation: Bushes last 10–15 years; replant on fresh ground.
